newsitem.title: ITALY: Details of Italy's revised 3-yr economic programme.
newsitem.headline: Details of Italy's revised 3-yr economic programme.

text.p: Following are the main objectives in the Italian government's three-year rolling financial targets (Dpef) which have been revised since the summer after the decision to increase 1997 budget deficit cuts.
Figures are in billion lire unless stated otherwise:

NOTE: The new Debt/GDP ratio data take into account only 37.5 trillion lire of the deficit cutting measures planned for next year and not the remaining 25 trillion lire of measures, including the "Euro tax", which have yet to be spelt out.
Trend public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) does not include any planned budget cutting measures.
Target PSBR does include planned budget deficit cuts, which can have a roll-over effect on the following years.
The government's deficit targets in the 1997/1999 Dpef are based on public sector accounts and not on public administration accounts.
The public administration deficit is the parameter used in the rest of Europe and by the Maastricht Treaty in its definition of criteria for entry into Europe's Economic and Monetary Union.

The new 1997 public administration deficit/GDP ratio goal is not indicated. It was previously set at 5.45 percent, compared with 4.5 percent for the original public sector deficit/GDP ratio. Undersecretary at the Treasury, Laura Pennacchi, said this week that both ratios would be around 3.0 pct in 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
